name: The Torus Universe in Three Dimensions
description: A locally flat vacuum cosmology with a compact spatial torus and evolving area and shape.
convention: Vacuum Einstein gravity in two spatial dimensions and one time dimension, with vanishing cosmological constant. The spatial topology is a torus, with two commuting Poincaré holonomies. The expanding and static sectors have flat spacetime curvature and distinct global identifications.
history: Emil Martinec quantized a universe with a torus for space in 1984 [martinec1984]. At each moment, its spatial metric was constant from point to point, with variables describing the area and shape of the whole torus. The constraints reduced the dynamics to finitely many degrees of freedom. The spacetime was locally flat, with no gravitational radiation [martinec1984].¶A flat spatial torus has a parallelogram as its fundamental domain. Corresponding points on opposite sides are the same point of space. Two side lengths and the angle between them determine its geometry; after fixing the area, two shape parameters remain [carlip1992torus]. A light ray can wind around its closed spatial directions.¶Edward Witten recast gravity in three dimensions as a Chern-Simons gauge theory in 1988 [witten1988]. For vanishing cosmological constant, its gauge group is the Poincaré group of Minkowski spacetime [carlip1992torus]. Transport around each independent torus circuit is described by a Poincaré transformation called a holonomy. Two commuting holonomies specify the torus identifications [carlip1992torus].¶In 1989 Vincent Moncrief expressed the vacuum dynamics of compact spatial surfaces as Hamiltonian evolution on Teichmüller space [moncrief1989]. For a torus, the Hamiltonian and its trajectories can be written explicitly. Akio Hosoya and Ken-ichi Nakao solved the initial data and evolution equations using surfaces whose mean extrinsic curvature is constant across space [hosoya_nakao1990]. The torus shape follows a geodesic in the hyperbolic upper half plane, with geometries related by modular transformations representing the same torus [hosoya_nakao1990, carlip1992torus].¶Steven Carlip expressed the changing torus shape directly in terms of its holonomies [carlip1992torus]. In the expanding family, two commuting generators combine boosts with translations along the transverse direction. The torus area grows linearly with proper time. Jorma Louko and Donald M. Marolf classified these expanding quotients alongside the static tori generated by two spatial translations [louko_marolf1994]. At the initial boundary of an expanding solution, the area tends to zero while spacetime remains flat at every positive proper time [louko_marolf1994, carlip2005].

coordinates.convention: The dimensionless coordinates $x$ and $y$ have period one, with $(x,y)\sim(x+1,y)\sim(x,y+1)$. The proper time is $t>0$, with $\Delta=a\mu-b\lambda>0$ and spatial area $A=ct\Delta$. The torus modulus is $m=(b+ict\mu)/(a+ict\lambda)$. Reversing the time orientation gives the contracting family.

coordinates.convention: The dimensionless coordinates $x$ and $y$ have period one, with $(x,y)\sim(x+1,y)\sim(x,y+1)$. The mean curvature coordinate is $\tau=1/(ct)$, decreasing toward the expanding future. Its modulus is $m=(b+i\mu/\tau)/(a+i\lambda/\tau)$ and its area is $A=(a\mu-b\lambda)/\tau$.

coordinates.convention: The developing map is $cT=ct\cosh q$, $X=ct\sinh q$, $Y=ax+by$, with $q=\lambda x+\mu y$. The first identification is $(cT,X,Y)\sim(cT\cosh\lambda+X\sinh\lambda,X\cosh\lambda+cT\sinh\lambda,Y+a)$. The second has $\mu$ and $b$ in place of $\lambda$ and $a$. Both act on the wedge $cT>|X|$, with $a\mu-b\lambda>0$.

coordinates.convention: The dimensionless coordinates $x$ and $y$ have period one, with $(x,y)\sim(x+1,y)\sim(x,y+1)$. For any reference length $\ell>0$, write $q=\lambda x+\mu y$, $cT=(\ell e^q+u e^{-q}/\ell)/2$, $X=(\ell e^q-u e^{-q}/\ell)/2$, and $Y=ax+by$. The area is $A=\sqrt{u}(a\mu-b\lambda)$, with $u>0$ and $a\mu-b\lambda>0$. The extension to $u<0$ has timelike tori.

coordinates.convention: The dimensionless coordinates $x$ and $y$ have period one, with $(x,y)\sim(x+1,y)\sim(x,y+1)$. The two spatial translations have lengths $r_1,r_2>0$ and angle $0<\varphi<\pi$. The constant modulus is $m=(r_2/r_1)e^{i\varphi}$ and the area is $A=r_1r_2\sin\varphi$.

related.text: Away from a point particle, the local geometry is the same flat vacuum in three dimensions. The torus universe closes space by two commuting identifications [carlip2005, louko_marolf1994].

The torus universe uses two commuting boost and translation identifications. An extension through its null boundary has timelike tori and closed timelike curves, as in Misner's boost quotient [louko_marolf1994].
The torus branch of Small Universes has three compact spatial directions. The torus universe in three dimensions has two and allows their global shape to evolve.
